descriptionHtml:
Approach · OAT-03 Retry/Timeout Resiliency · S09 Haiku times out on Ask AI (slow, not a fast error): the fallback answers, and the log puts the lost 20 s on the AI service (both contexts)

UAT steps / ticket ACs covered:

  • U5 When the primary model (Haiku) is forced to fail or time out, Haiku is retried once, then the same call goes to Mistral (UAT OAT-03 step 6; UAT OAT-03 Expected Result 3; TFA-94422 AC 2)
  • T3 The full retry sequence stays within about 30 s (TFA-94422 AC 7; UAT 3.5)
  • U1 When the network drops or an AI provider times out mid-dictation or mid-note-generation, the app retries automatically rather than hanging indefinitely; … (UAT OAT-03 step 1; UAT OAT-03 step 2; UAT OAT-03 Expected Result 1; UAT 3.5; TFA-94745 AC 4; TFA-92568 AC 5)
  • U8 Each run logs how long the AI call itself took, separately from the total, so a slow run can be traced to the AI service or to the app (UAT 3.5)
  • U13 All of the above in both Hospital and Nursing Home, on web, iOS and Android (UAT 3.3; UAT Empty & Failure States Expected Result; TFA-94745 AC 6)

Test design technique: Boundary values (boundary) — Sit right on the edge of the rule (exactly on time / a minute late, empty, longest, most) and see on which side the behavior changes.

Given Local stack with Haiku made to hang until its 20 s attempt deadline (an AbortError, counted as temporary); Mistral answers normally

When Ask 'What medications is the patient on?' 5 times for QA Hosp Okafor (Hospital) and 5 times for QA Resident Brooks (Nursing Home)

Then Each answer comes from Mistral (fellBackFrom Haiku) and names the medications on file; each assist.askChart row has providerMs ≥ 20000 (the hung Haiku attempt counts as the AI service's time) and durationMs − providerMs ≤ about 2000 (the 1 s retry pause plus overhead), so the slow run is put on the AI service (3.5); …

Pass rule (oracle, excerpt): mustInclude per fixture. Backend check on each assist.askChart row, read right after the call: model = Mistral, fellBackFrom = Haiku, providerMs ≥ 20000 (the hung Haiku attempt counts as the AI service's time) and durationMs − providerMs ≤ about 2000 (the 1 s retry pause plus overhead). …

Where it ran: local aicheck-other (AI output checks); test method API · API (Convex functions); lane planned in the matrix: AI check (blocked)

S09 is our own case number (its number in the coverage matrix cases/OAT-03.matrix.json), not a step number of the UAT document.

Triage (2026-10-14): 1 row.

Issue type: Test issue · environment local · tickets TFA-92568 in progress; TFA-94422 ready for qa; TFA-94745 ready for qa

Not judged: the Haiku-timeout-on-Ask-AI case needs a Bedrock proxy that makes Haiku hang, wired in with env set on a private backend, which waits for Quinn's OK.

Evidence: allure bb2b50cf-…-result.json; aicheck-other 'blocked'. bedrock-proxy.mjs (Haiku hangs or returns 429 after N ms; Mistral is re-signed and forwarded) passed an offline self-test; it needs AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_BEDROCK_RUNTIME on the private backend, the same env-set gate as S07. Not run.

Environment: local — main e02167f, local stack (not a deployed build); run folder runs/2026-10-14-local, lane aicheck-other.

Test method: API · API (Convex functions); secondary: FAULT · Fault injection — as classified in cases/test-methods.json, which says it runs on local; Source: aicheck-other.

UAT item: OAT-03 Retry/Timeout Resiliency · Section: B · Operational Acceptance Tests · Scenario: OAT-03/S09

Haiku times out on Ask AI (slow, not a fast error): the fallback answers, and the log puts the lost 20 s on the AI service (both contexts)

Tickets: TFA-92568 Phase 4: Make it safe for real patients (in progress); TFA-94422 Haiku primary, Mistral fallback via Bedrock (ready for qa); TFA-94745 Empty & Failure States (ready for qa)

New local lane aicheck-other: status blocked in aicheck-other/results.json → blocked (blocked).

How it is tested (aicheck-other/plan.json, automatable: partly): Fault backend + a local Bedrock proxy (AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_BEDROCK_RUNTIME on the fault backend only): Haiku requests hang until the SDK's 20 s abort; Mistral requests are re-signed and forwarded to Bedrock unchanged. 5 Hospital + 5 Nursing Home askChart calls (context as AskModal.tsx, temporal line included); per row model=Mistral, fellBackFrom=Haiku, providerMs >= 20000, durationMs - providerMs <= ~2000; question-to-answer over 30 s flagged; Haiku second try recorded from the proxy's request log (not judged, Q4). — The fault seams are deployment env vars (BEDROCK_TEST_FAIL_MODEL in convex/ai/providers/bedrock.ts; AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_BEDROCK_RUNTIME → bedrock-proxy.mjs for hang / 429-after-N). Setting them needs `convex env set`, which CLAUDE.md forbids without exception, and the shared stack must never carry them. Built and harness-checked; the run waits for Quinn's OK to use env set on a private backend (fault-stack.sh, QA_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ENV=1).

Detail:

Needs Haiku to hang to its 20 s attempt deadline. No seam on main; built a network-level one instead of a code change: bedrock-proxy.mjs (AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_BEDROCK_RUNTIME on the private backend only; Haiku requests hang or get a 429 after N ms, Mistral is re-signed and forwarded; per-request log for the Haiku second-try count, Q4). Self-tested offline: 429 after 600 ms, and a hang held until the client aborted. Pointing the backend at it needs `convex env set` (same gate as S07). ask-ai-fault.ts S09 checks providerMs >= 20000 and durationMs - providerMs <= ~2 s per row and flags > 30 s. Context now built exactly as AskModal.tsx (temporal line folded in), as for S07.

Evidence: 0 attached; 2 not attached:

  • scripts/aicheck-other/bedrock-proxy.mjs — outside the local run folder, not attached
  • scripts/aicheck-other/ask-ai-fault.ts — outside the local run folder, not attached

Dev run: skipped: local-only — local-only — Not a dev lane C: it needs a local-only seam that makes Haiku hang to its 20 s attempt deadline (fault-ai), and its providerMs / durationMs checks are about that hung attempt.. This local result replaces that dev entry (the scenario appears once).
